## Reporting CFAs 

- Specification & theoretical motivation
- Assumptions: linearity, multicollinearity, 
- Distributions: Skew, kurtosis, estimator used
- Covariance matrix + means
- Path diagram (with & without estimates)
- Free parameters/identification
- Standard model fit paramters
- Path estimates, residual covariances, etc
  - Standardized & unstandardized

- Which items are NOT relevant to CFA? 

## Reporting Workshop Part 1

- Teams of 3-4 people
- Act as reviewers: Is this report ready for publication/presentation? 
  - each team has a different report
  - Write a detailed review (see next slide)
  - Make a determination: Is this paper publishable or does it need a revise & resubmit? 

## Reviewing a paper for publication

1. Highlevel comments on overall quality: relevance of the question to the field; apprpriateness of the methods; any discrepancies between RQ, methods, results, discussion;  summary of things the paper does well; summary of areas for improvement.

## Reviewing a paper for publication

2. Substance
  - line or section specific feedback: Well-organized support for the RQ, assumptions missing.  
3. Minor typos 
  - Mismatching numbers between tables/text, misspellings, grammar

## Review Decision

  - Accept: minor edits like typos; no substantive issues
  - Revise & resubmit: Relevant to the field, conceptually the methods address the RQ; results & discussion follow logically. May be some misinterpretations, missing analyses that need done, etc. 
  - Reject: RQ not relevant to the field, major logical problems in which the methods don't address the RQ, etc. 

## Reporting workshop Part 2

- 1 representative from each team
- Each person explains their team's project (< 1 minute each)
- Each person highlights specific feebdack to the author (Major -> minor)
